note: OBSERVATION: 93.6% skip rate even at max_tokens=384 on structured output. The wide rollout budget shaves a few points off the floor (cap #2 was 97%) but doesn't eliminate it. The remaining skips come from the unfixed rollout-prompt-construction issue (orig_input_ids[..first_label] ending before assistant cue marker).

OBSERVATION: tool-call capability shows clean target sub-score lift (+16.67pp on required_fields) without confound on length_band — the rubric design has no length sub-score, so OPD's preferred shortcut (length compression) isn't available here. Structured tasks WITHOUT a length sub-score = clean target movement.

FEATURE VALIDATION: OpdPrompt.teacher_extra_messages (shipped earlier this session, commit 46087c4e) works correctly. First real use: 26 prompts, 268-token avg teacher prefix, 6 epochs. Mechanism confirmed: structural-output skip-rate floor eliminated entirely (93.6%→~0%). Adapter not produced (run killed at 39% completion). Best-so-far for cap #4 remains iter 1's symmetric adapter at composite 0.8939.

KILN GAP: OPD trainer has no intermediate adapter checkpoint. cuda_opd_remote saves only at run completion. Killing mid-run = losing all LoRA state. Should add a SIGUSR1 handler that triggers save-current-LoRA, or periodic checkpoint every N steps. Tracked separately.

SKILL IMPROVEMENT: hypotheses should include a wall-time budget. iter 2's 156 nominal × ~150s/step = 6.5h wasn't anticipated at hypothesis time. The H9 design correctly removed the skip-rate floor that made iter 1 fast; the hypothesis-author didn't reckon with the inverse implication on wall time. Next session: hypothesis.md template should ask 'wall-time budget'.

CHECKPOINT FEATURE VALIDATED: shipped same session, first real test. 6 checkpoints written reliably at step 25/50/75/100/125/150 during the 6h13m run. Critically, the BEST checkpoint (75) was NOT the final adapter — without checkpointing we'd have only the catastrophic 0.343 final adapter and missed the 0.792 mid-training adapter entirely. The 'stop once things plateau' user requirement is real and the feature delivers it.

OPD FAILURE MODE: EOS collapse from over-trained asymmetric. Teacher's distribution sharply weights JSON shape; <|im_end|> never gets enough mass; student internalizes 'always emit JSON'. Mitigations to consider in kiln: (a) include a small SFT mix on response endings (Stable-OPD style λ·SFT_gold), (b) add an entropy regularizer that penalizes near-zero entropy distributions, (c) cap max_tokens during training to force EOS into the active span. Mitigations in skill: H9 hypothesis template should specify a step budget that's INVERSELY proportional to teacher-distribution sharpness.

RUBRIC GOODHART HOLE: this capability's `parses` sub-score uses best-effort JSON extraction (extracts first balanced {...} and tries to parse). It gives partial credit to 'valid JSON followed by garbage'. A strict-only-JSON sub-score would have made the EOS collapse hit the floor faster and clearer. Next capability: apply the §0 adversarial-design review more carefully — explicitly ask 'does any sub-score still pass when the model emits valid CONTENT followed by stopping-failure?'

VLLM CONFIG WIN: --enable-prefix-caching defaults OFF in vLLM 0.17 (verified mid-session — our 6h13m asymmetric run had 'Prefix cache hit rate: 0.0%' for all 156 effective steps). Flipping it on saves ~54% latency on the OPD-shape prompt_logprobs query when the same teacher prefix is reused across epochs. For asymmetric OPD specifically (the cap-#4 iter-3 shape), that's ~30-40s saved per step → 6h13m → ~4-5h. Skill §6 now requires the flag; templates/teacher-up.sh ships with it.
